chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: George Brunis refuses to help
summary: Brunis, nicknamed Iron Head, will not help the new leader, while Pee Wee was kind; later they work together for years.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: There is some rumor - you know - the rumor I'm talking about reported something that you and Brunis had some kind of squabble and that's why he left Nick's after you came in as a new leader; remember, you were a kid to him because you used to hang around and watch him play in Chicago---
Well, I needed some help from these

guys - Pee Wee was helpful, you know, Pee Wee was always a sweet guy but Brunis was a stubborn bastard-- you know, really -- the reason they called him "Iron Head" wasn't for nothing -- because that's exactly what he was--- and, he refused to help me and I just had to fight it my own way. I was doing all right, but I was making lots of mistakes and he could have straightened me out if he wanted to but he refused to do it and, of course, I worked with him years later too---
You spent many years - and made some of your greatest recordings with Brunis---

Yes - we were always friendly -- as friends go but he never was any help to me, you know, most guys were very helpful to me and helped me with something I didn't know but not Brunis. That's why when Brad Gowans came in - oh, was he helpful and a sweet guy and played like hell; he was a marvelous player.
